title: Anybody Headed Down Today?
intro: Sunday morning. Priya's on her break on the deck at Stamford Coffee, checking her phone every few minutes.
smallTalk: Priya's boy has a showcase in the city tonight. Half the village knows already.
Walt's truck is on J&H's lot with the hood up.
The trail's dry the whole way to Hobart this week.
Tops has the good peaches in.
Soggiest summer anybody up here can remember.
Nice to see everybody pitching in for Priya's boy.
Somebody's fixing up the space under Stamford Coffee. Nobody will say what.
The self-serve fridge at Stamford Coffee has dinner in it, if you're late home.
80 Main has the Catskills sweaters in again.

items.name: Priya's costume bag
items.blurb: Half a dance costume, sequins and all.

items.name: Jess R.'s jumper cables
items.blurb: Red and black, coiled neat, out of the back of her truck.

lines: It got there? He sent me a photo from the stage door. Sequins and all.
Thank you.
You found cables! Good. Walt will get going yet.
Walt's battery is dead? That truck.
Somebody round here will have cables.
Did you find someone going down?
Sorry — I keep looking at my phone. My son's dance showcase is in the city tonight, and half his costume is in this bag. I left it out of his case.
I'm working here till four, and it's three hours down. He needs it by five.
If you come across anyone driving down today — would you take this with you and ask around?
You found cables? Good. Now anyone with a car will do. I just need one parked next to mine for a bit.
Still dead. Cables first, then a car next to mine.
Priya's bag? Sure, I'll take it down. I go every other Sunday. Put it on the seat.
Only I'm not going anywhere yet. Battery's dead, and my cables are at home.
Jess usually helps me out. She keeps a set in her truck.
The truck? Battery's dead. I'm waiting on a jump.
Walt's truck started? Good.
You found them. Get those to Walt at J&H.
Jess R.? The south end of the trail, where the old rail bed starts.
Cables? You've got the wrong Jess. I don't keep any.
There's a Jess who walks the rail trail on Sundays, and one down in Hobart, by the bridge.
Morning. Waiting on the mail.
He got started? Good.
Go on, get those to Walt. I've eleven miles to walk.
Cables? For Walt? I've a set in the truck. Here.
Get them to him. He's waiting.

effects.toast: You've got Jess R.'s jumper cables.

lines: The rail trail? Eleven miles to Hobart and not a hill on it. You can hear the creek most of the way.
Walt got his jump? Good.
Walt got going? Good.
Get those to Walt. Then he needs someone with a car to sit with him, and mine's at home.
Cables? Not me. Try the Jess on the trail, or the one on Main Street in Stamford.
Cables? Wrong Jess — I don't have a set.
There's a Jess who walks the rail trail from Stamford on Sundays, and one on Main Street up there.
This spot? Best one in Hobart. The water does all the talking.
Walt? He got off fine. I hope the costume made it in time for the show.
Give it a few minutes.
You've got cables? Then I've got the car. Come on.
Walt's battery? I'd pull the wagon round, only I've no cables either.

Walt will have said Jess, and there's more than one of us. There's a Jess on Main Street in Stamford, one who walks the rail trail on Sundays, and one down in Hobart by the bridge. One of them will have a set.
Me? Coffee on the patio and nothing I have to do.
Did the bag make it?
Got them? Get those up to Walt.
Walt needs a jump? Jess has jumper cables.
Somebody driving down today? Walt goes every other Sunday, and it's his Sunday. He'll be up at J&H in Jefferson.
Morning! Coffee's on.
Priya was in earlier asking if anyone's driving to the city today. She's over at the coffee shop.
It worked out? Good. Come by for a tasting sometime.
Jess R.'s cables? Get those to Walt.
Walt needs a jump? Jess T., by the bridge, might know who has cables.
Driving to the city? Not me today — my truck's in the shop. Walt goes every other Sunday, up in Jefferson.
Welcome. Pull up a seat on the bench any time.
Walt got away? Tell Priya's boy break a leg from all of us in here.
Walt's battery? Somebody came in saying so. He'll be fine.
Downstairs? Still no idea. There's paper over the window now.
Sit anywhere.
Have you heard about the space underneath us? Somebody's been hammering down there all week. Nobody knows what it is.
If I had to guess, a gallery. Half the people at these tables paint.
Downstairs? I still say oysters.
Don't mind me — I'm deciding between two sweaters.
The work under the coffee shop? The whole town's noticed. Nobody knows what it is.
My guess is an oyster bar. The wine nights in here fill right up.
Downstairs? Still no answer. Biscuit sniffs at that window every walk.
Morning. This is Biscuit. He checks the patio before we go anywhere, so we check the patio.
The space under the coffee shop? Somebody's doing it up. Paper on the window and hammering behind it.
My guess is dog treats. Every dog in Stamford naps on this deck.
Red to red, black on the bracket. Now leave it running.
Give it a few minutes.
There it is. Listen to that.
Thanks, Jess.

steps.toast: Episode complete — new story next week

lines: Taped inside the door: "The truck on the lot is Walt's. He's waiting on a jump."
Pinned to the board by the door: somebody's asking if anybody's headed down to the city tonight. Two people have written "ask Walt" underneath, in two different pens.

A stairwell goes down under the building here, plywood laid across the bottom of it and brown paper taped over the little window beside the top step. Somebody is at work down there — you can hear a saw.
Not a word written on any of it.
